sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *según* for citing a source from B1 Unit 13, *por lo visto* from B2 Unit 3 and the impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 6. All of them put a claim on someone else's shoulders: you report it, but you do not say that it is true. This lesson adds three more tools for the same job, and shows you a news form to recognise.

sections.title: Reporting from a distance
rows: Según el vecino, la tienda cerró.
Al parecer, el director ya había salido.
Supuestamente, el contrato ya estaba firmado.
Dio a entender que sabía más.
Se dice que la tienda cerró el mes pasado.

sections.title: Saying it, or passing it on
sections.content: Compare *El río había subido mucho* (you say it is so) with *Según una vecina, el río había subido mucho* or *Al parecer, el río había subido mucho* (you pass it on). These tools are followed by the indicative, because you are reporting what is said or seen, not rejecting it. *Supuestamente* and *presunto* go further: they suggest that the claim may not be true.

sections.title: A form to recognise
sections.content: In newspapers you will meet a conditional used to pass on a rumour: *El ministro habría dicho que no vendría* ("The minister reportedly said that he would not come"). The conditional tells you that the writer reports it without confirming it. Some Spanish style guides advise against it in careful writing, but you will see it in the news, so learn to recognise it. You do not need to use it.

items.spanish: Según el vecino, el río subió mucho anoche.
items.english: According to the neighbour, the river rose a lot last night.

items.spanish: Al parecer, el director ya había salido de la oficina.
items.english: Apparently, the director had already left the office.

items.spanish: El presunto culpable negó haber estado allí.
items.english: The alleged culprit denied having been there.

items.spanish: Se dice que la tienda cerró el mes pasado.
items.english: It is said that the shop closed last month.

sections.content: Pick the tool by what you want to say: a named source (*según*), something you saw or read (*al parecer*, *por lo visto*), or a claim you doubt (*supuestamente*, *presunto*).
